content.value_statement: Slow database queries can increase costs and make applications feel unreliable. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review queries, execution plans, and index choices.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SQL queries for full table scans, inefficient joins, and missing indexes.
Explains EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output for PostgreSQL and MySQL examples.
Suggests index types, composite indexes, covering indexes, and partial indexes.
Identifies N+1 query patterns and recommends eager loading or join-based alternatives.
Provides slow-query monitoring guidance using pg_stat_statements and MySQL tools.
limitations: It cannot prove performance gains without real execution plans and representative data.
It does not replace database-specific testing before production changes.
Index recommendations can improve reads while slowing writes and increasing storage use.
It depends on the query, schema, indexes, and database version supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Tune a Slow Endpoint
use_cases.description: Review a query behind a slow API route and get practical indexing or rewrite ideas.

use_cases.title: Review Database Indexes
use_cases.description: Compare current indexes with common query patterns and find missing, duplicate, or unused indexes.

use_cases.title: Improve Analytics Queries
use_cases.description: Analyze reporting queries, joins, filters, and aggregation patterns before they reach production workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SQL query for performance. Explain likely bottlenecks, needed indexes, and safer rewrite options. Query: [paste query]. Schema and row counts: [paste details].

prompt_templates.title: Explain an Execution Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this execution plan and explain the most expensive operations in plain language. Then suggest changes to test first. Plan: [paste EXPLAIN output].

prompt_templates.title: Find ORM Query Problems
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this ORM data access pattern for N+1 queries, unnecessary fields, and inefficient joins. Suggest an improved loading strategy. Context: [paste code or description].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Tuning Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized optimization plan for these slow queries. Include expected impact, index tradeoffs, verification steps, and rollback considerations. Inputs: [queries, plans, schema, workload notes].

output_examples.input: A user shares a slow customer lookup query plus table size, current indexes, and an execution plan.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a full table scan, recommends a targeted email index, explains why selectivity matters, and lists verification steps.

output_examples.input: A developer describes loading users and then loading orders inside a loop.
output_examples.output: The skill flags an N+1 pattern, recommends eager loading or a join-based aggregate, and explains how query count changes.

output_examples.input: A team provides a list of slow reporting queries and current index definitions.
output_examples.output: The skill groups issues by missing indexes, excessive selected columns, pagination cost, and monitoring gaps.

best_practices: Provide schema, row counts, current indexes, and execution plans with every query review.
Test each suggested change on production-like data before changing production systems.
Measure before and after optimization so improvements are tied to evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not add every suggested index without checking write cost and storage impact.
Do not optimize from query text alone when an execution plan is available.
Do not apply database-specific syntax without confirming the target database version.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers common SQL tuning patterns for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, and SQLite.

faq.question: Can it run queries for me?
faq.answer: The skill provides analysis guidance. Query execution depends on the tools and database access available in your environment.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Share the query, schema, row counts, indexes, database version, and EXPLAIN output when possible.

faq.question: Will every recommendation make queries faster?
faq.answer: No. Performance depends on data distribution, workload, indexes, and database settings. Always test changes.

faq.question: Does it help with ORM performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for N+1 query patterns, eager loading, and selecting only needed fields.

faq.question: Can it review index maintenance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for unused indexes, duplicate indexes, and rebuilding or analyzing indexes.
